reasons.reader_question: The chapter leaves two clear questions: why unspent Varanad silver sits in a raider scout's purse, and whether Devan's pepper-store cat line means he knows. It loses a point because the coin's importance belongs to Devan's silence, not to Neela's own inference.
reasons.change: Knowledge changes (new coin, a second tally reaches Devan), relationship changes (she becomes his protector by choice) and power changes (he now knows someone stood on the ledge before him and holds that over the table).
reasons.romance_movement: The reason is new: her first chosen act of protection, made against a clean exit, answered by his sideways thanks. The leads share only two short scenes, so most of the movement is indirect and works.
reasons.shown_chemistry: Shown through responsive action, not narration: 'Then I'll look at it asleep', his mouth going still when pleased, the fish dish pushed to her side without a glance, the milk for the cat. Neela waiting for his breath hitch adds to it. None of it is narrated chemistry.
reasons.character_logic: Neela's reasoning for the satchel and her refusal of the hunger are smart and fit her character. Devan riding a day after septic fever is stubborn, but the Raman motive justifies it. The ridge timing ('stars came out' then 'four hours to first light') blurs her watch.
reasons.stakes_and_cost: Saving him costs her the cleanest road in twelve contracts, a second empty cup at the stone, an unexplained missed Valli, and a night of hunger unfed. The costs are counted on the ridge but not yet felt as consequences, and the dawn danger is defused before the reader fears it.
reasons.prose: Concrete and well voiced ('like the bite in a flatbread', 'It was a lie, and it was a good one. She used it.'). The ridge sum has muddled lines ('It came out the same'; 'who would be dead by a stranger's hand and save her the trouble'), and 'twelve days' echoes. No banned phrases or AI tells found.
reasons.continuity: Consistent with F083, F085, F119, F129-F136, F133, F134 and F371-F373. The night count (28) fits ch13 (29) and ch15 (20 nights, eight later). Devan avoids the night-shape word ('A cat'). The Muthu glance is a soft risk, but it is Neela's inference, not a stated fact.

fixes: Technique 6 (Probable-but-Uncertain) is tagged but underpowered: Neela defuses the ambush at night, so the dawn patrol carries almost no suspense. Rework the terrace passage at 'Birds were already turning above the lip of the cliff' so the threat is probable and specific. For example, she sees a second figure come over the far ridge beyond the cut and start down toward the dark camp while the column is still bunched on the shelf, then loses him in the scrub. Hold that uncertainty until the riders come home by the cart road.

The ridge sum loses clarity at 'She counted it all, to the last coin. It came out the same.' and at 'who would be dead by a stranger's hand and save her the trouble'. A reader can't tell which way the sum points, and the second clause argues for letting him die inside the 'other side' paragraph, which is about the costs of intervening. Fix both: end the costs paragraph on a cost, and make the result explicit (for example: 'Every column said lie still.'). Also fix the time jump after 'She lay there while the stars came out' by marking the hours passing ('The cistern chain came up faint from the fort, once, twice...') before 'Four hours to first light'.

At 'Her eyes went, without her leave, to Muthu's big, open, listening face' the chapter points Neela, and through her Devan, at Muthu ten chapters early. Devan still believes Muthu (F117) and the inside-informant inference belongs to ch24 (F220). Spending that suspicion now weakens the later payoff. Have her glance take in the whole hall instead (Chinna at the kitchen door, the servers, the open door to the yard), so the reader suspects someone in the house without Muthu being singled out.
reader_question: Why would raider scouts carry freshly minted, never-handled Varanad silver, and does Devan's 'the pepper-store cat has been busy' mean he knows it was her?
new_facts_assessment: F371 (revised satchel motive) is necessary and an improvement. It removes the impossible knowledge of Asha's note and grounds the drop in the hall tally Neela saw herself, which fits F049-F050 and F112-F113. F372 (counting the cost of a second missed stone) is needed to make technique 18 cost something, and it fits F087, F122, F127 and F133. F373 (Devan shows only the coin's edge and says 'I won't answer that' to Muthu) fits his voice and sets up the inside-informant thread. It must not be read as Devan already suspecting Muthu, since F117 has him believing Muthu until ch24 (F217).
